Subject: On-prem planning: quick site inventory + approach for host profiles and PVC placement

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for taking time today. To make the PoC smooth and to avoid surprises when we spin up the private deployment in your data center, could you confirm the short inventory items below? We want to produce a concrete node profile matrix and an I/O/egress plan.

Requested inventory (attachment welcome):
- Number of physical hosts available per site, with CPU, RAM, and local NVMe or SSD counts.
- Rack-to-top-of-rack networking (switch speeds), and whether hosts have dual NICs for management vs data plane.
- Current outbound egress path (NAT box / firewall) and any per-subnet restrictions to public endpoints.
- Storage availability: Is there SAN/NFS/Ceph already? Any preference for block (iSCSI) vs file?
- K8s control plane preference: customer-mananged or Redwood-managed inside a VPC peering?

Our initial plan (what we want to validate against your inventory):
- Node pools: dedicated inference (GPU) pool(s) + control/infra pool (no GPUs) + storage gateway pool (if using local NVMe for cache).
- PVC placement: prefer persistent network storage for model artifacts and long-term state; local NVMe can be used for KV/cache layer to reduce latency for hot prefixes.
- Network: route inference egress through a dedicated NAT and allowlist Redwood control-plane IPs; keep telemetry paths outbound-only.

I attached a simple template for site inventory — fill what you have and we can iterate.

Next step: if you can return the inventory by EOD tomorrow we’ll produce a proposed node profile PDF and a brief set of firewall rules you can hand to networking.

Thanks,

Hi Marcus —

Nice inventory; comfortable approach. Concise recommendations below for the PoC:

1) PVC and artifact placement
- Use NetApp NFS for model artifacts, checkpoints, and anything that needs durability across cluster lifecycle. Provision a dedicated export with NFSv4 and enable root-squash per RavenBank policy.
- Use local NVMe as ephemeral cache for the runtime KV (sharded per pod). Mount as hostPath + lvm-thin logical volume if you want simple size quotas (we usually create a small LV per pod and map via device-mapper).
- For pods that require persistence across restarts but benefit from low latency, consider an approach where on pod start we prefetch model shards from NFS into NVMe cache and mark last-modified metadata on NFS. If a node fails, pod restart will rehydrate from NFS to another node's NVMe.

2) Eviction and replication for KV/cache
- Treat NVMe cache as ephemeral LRU; use a TTL-based eviction at application layer plus a periodic checksum to reconcile with NFS. No writes of canonical state to NVMe (write-through to NFS for anything canonical).
- For critical per-request working-state, enable replication at app layer across pods in different nodes (anti-affinity).

3) Node pool sizing and taints
- infra: 3 nodes, 32GB RAM, tainted infra=true:NoSchedule, labelled redwood/infra=yes.
- control: if customer-managing control plane, aim for 3 controllers in Site A (keep odd number); Site B can host standby etc.
- infer-gpu: size hosts to optimize GPU memory and PCIe lanes — if using 8x A10 equivalents, target 48-64GB host RAM per GPU; schedule 1 inference pod per GPU to keep latency predictable.
- storage-proxy: 2 nodes with NVMe: use PodDisruptionBudget=1 and tolerate NoExecute for short-term maintenance.

4) Networking and egress
- Outbound: Redwood control-plane calls should be allowed to a small set of IP ranges (we'll provide a CIDR block). Arrange a pre-approved change window to add allowlist.
- DNS: ensure cluster nodes can resolve redwood-inference endpoints (we prefer explicit egress DNS via their recursive resolvers).
- MTU: keep MTU >= 9000 if using SR-IOV or jumbo frames for high throughput; confirm with ravenbank networking.

5) Monitoring / SLOs during PoC
- We will deploy lightweight tracing and token-level telemetry outbound-only. Keep telemetry egress via the same NAT.

6) Alternatives if Ops blocks NFS changes
- If NetApp export cannot be dedicated, propose an S3 gateway inside the cluster (minio or S3-compatible fronting the NetApp) or object-store in-site. This adds latency but avoids SAN changes.

I can turn the above into a one-page matrix and firewall rule snippet for Samir. Any additional constraints (change window length, maintenance blackout) we should add?

— Neha
Neha Kapoor
Principal Infra Architect, Redwood Inference

Samir —

Appreciate the fast turn around and the inventory. Based on Neha's notes (key excerpts below) here's the short PoC plan and next steps so your networking and ops teams have a concrete checklist: 

PoC plan (summary):
- Model artifacts: NetApp NFS export (dedicated), mount via NFSv4 on a redwood-models namespace.
- Hot cache: use hostPath->lvm thin volumes on NVMe for per-pod KV cache. Application will use write-through to NFS for canonical state.
- Node pools: infra (3), control (3 customer-managed), infer-gpu (start 2 hosts, scale to 6), storage-proxy (2 with NVMe).
- Egress/Firewall: allowlist Redwood control-plane IPs (we will provide CIDRs). Open outbound ports: 443 (HTTPS), 5222 (if you want agent control channel), and DNS (53 UDP/TCP to your recursive resolver).
- MTU: recommend >=9000 on data VLAN for inference traffic.

Attachments: I attached a short PDF with node profile recommendations and a 1-page firewall rule snippet: ri-proposed-node-profiles-20260809.pdf

Requested from RavenBank (action items):
1) Confirm you can provision a dedicated NFS export and the change window for allowlisting Redwood IPs.
2) Confirm preferred GPU SKU (we will provide options A100/A30 equivalent pricing); for the PoC we can start on A10-equivalent.
3) Approve the proposed node counts so we can schedule a two-hour maintenance window to deploy the PoC cluster.

If all good, we’ll schedule the deployment for next week and provide a short runbook for your ops team.

Thanks,
Marcus
